Export a plot to a 3D model, vector or source-code file

Source: R/export-3d.R
export_3d.Rd

Writes the scene of a plot to a file that other software opens. Model formats hold the scene of one panel in 3D: glTF binary (.glb) or glTF with a separate buffer (.gltf and .bin) for Blender and the web, PLY, OBJ with an MTL material file, binary STL and 3MF. Faces are triangulated, paths become tubes or line primitives, and points become small solids or point primitives, all in model coordinates: the panel box scaled by the aspect of coord_3d(), with its longest side size long; 3MF and STL written with print hold millimetre solids instead. Vector and source formats hold the projected plot: SVG with source rows and hover text, TikZ (.tex) and an Asymptote scene (.asy).

Usage

export_3d(
  plot,
  file = NULL,
  format = NULL,
  panel = 1L,
  furniture = FALSE,
  lines = c("tube", "line"),
  points = c("mesh", "point"),
  size = 1,
  width = 640L,
  height = 640L,
  dpi = 96,
  print = NULL,
  interactive = TRUE,
  standalone = TRUE,
  prc = FALSE
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot with coord_3d().

file

Output path, or NULL to use format. Its extension selects the format: .glb, .gltf, .ply, .obj, .stl, .3mf, .svg, .tex (TikZ) or .asy.

format

Output format as one of these extension names. With file = NULL, the format writes to a session temporary path. When both are supplied, the extension of file must agree with format.

panel

Panel index in layout order, default 1, for model formats and Asymptote; SVG and TikZ hold every panel.

furniture

Whether to include the panes, grid lines and box edges, default FALSE.

lines

"tube" (default) writes each path as a closed tube with the drawn line width as diameter; "line" writes line primitives.

points

"mesh" (default) writes each point as a solid of its drawn size: a cube for square shapes, a tetrahedron for triangles, an octahedron for diamonds and a sphere for the other shapes; "point" writes point primitives.

size

Length of the longest side of the box in file units, default 1.

width, height

Device size in pixels used to lay out the plot, default 640 each. Tubes and solids keep the size relative to the box that lines and points have in a plot of this size.

dpi

Device resolution, default 96 dots per inch.

print

A print_3d() specification for closed millimetre solids: optional for STL, required for 3MF.

interactive

SVG: whether to include tooltips, keyboard focus and linked hover highlighting for fragments of the same source row.

standalone

TikZ: whether to include a LaTeX document preamble.

prc

Asymptote: whether to include PRC in its PDF output.

Value

The written path, invisibly.

Details

glTF output follows the glTF 2.0 specification and is the route into Blender, whose importer reads its meshes, materials, cameras and animation. The vertical axis of the plot becomes +y. Each layer is one named node (layer1_point, layer2_surface, ...), and the furniture is a node furniture with the children panes, grid and box, so layers can be selected, hidden and restyled after import. Mapped colours are vertex colours (COLOR_0, linear light), so a colour scale needs no material per colour. Faces drawn with lighting (light_3d() and shade) use one lit material whose base colour multiplies the vertex colours; all other geometry uses the KHR_materials_unlit extension. Translucent geometry uses alpha blending and every material is double sided. A node camera holds the view of the panel, so the file opens on the plot's view; an oblique projection is written as an orthographic camera along the sight direction. animate_3d() writes animated glTF files.

PLY output is binary with vertex normals and 8-bit sRGB vertex colours; line primitives are edge elements. OBJ output writes one object per node, sRGB vertex colours after each vertex position, and one MTL material per distinct colour; its vertical axis is +y, as OBJ importers expect. PLY and STL keep the vertical axis of the plot as +z. STL holds triangles only, so it requires lines = "tube" and points = "mesh".

Ordinary model exports omit text and write dashed lines solid. Printing exports include extruded text according to print_3d().

SVG output writes the compiled, depth-ordered fragments as SVG geometry. Each fragment carries data-layer, data-row and data-primitive attributes. Consecutive runs of each layer share a group so that interleaved layers retain their visibility order. Scene masks become clipping paths, and surface seams share compound-path underlays. Static plot furniture is embedded as SVG. A tooltip aesthetic sets the hover text.

TikZ writes the complete SVG paint order as editable fill, draw and text commands, including clip paths, furniture and legends. Requires TikZ's svg.path library. Raster colourbars and annotations become coloured pixel rectangles using the optional png decoder. TeX selects the text font. Asymptote writes model-space triangles, paths, marker solids, text and a camera, so it can re-render the scene from another view or produce an interactive PRC PDF. For a PRC PDF, compile with asy -tex pdflatex -f pdf plot.asy and install the TeX packages media9 and ocgx2. A PDF reader with PRC support supplies the interactive view.

See also

animate_3d() for animated glTF files.

Examples

d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 15), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 15))
d$z <- d$x * exp(-d$x^2 - d$y^2)
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(ggplot2::aes(fill = z)) + coord_3d()
glb <- export_3d(p, tempfile(fileext = ".glb"))
file.size(glb)
export_3d(p, tempfile(fileext = ".stl"), size = 50)
asy <- export_3d(p, format = "asy")
if (requireNamespace("svglite", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("xml2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  export_3d(p, format = "svg")
  export_3d(p, format = "tex", standalone = FALSE)
}
